title: FORECAST.ETS fits histories of four or fewer points nonseasonally and extends those under seven by regression
statement: In DNA Calc's implementation of FORECAST.ETS, every prepared history of four or fewer points is fitted as a nonseasonal series, whether the seasonality argument is automatic (1), an explicit 2, or 0. For a history shorter than seven points the starting series is extended to seven points before the search: the trend is the least-squares slope of the points in order (computed in plain binary64), and the point at index j (from the history length up to 6) is y[j mod 2] + (j - j mod 2) * trend. DNA Calc computed these histories under this rule and matched Excel on 199 of the 204 recorded short-history cells; the other five differ from Excel by 1 to 3 units in the last place. One recorded Excel forecast, FORECAST.ETS(5, {2,7,-1,4}, {1,2,3,4}, 2) = 1.5926883521785709, is held as a unit test. Before this change the same histories were refused unless the slope and every product and sum were exact in binary64; on the oracle corpus the passed count went from 76,480 to 76,759 and the refused count from 956 to 672, with no previously matched row lost.
basis: The row counts (199 of 204 cells, +279 passed, +5 mismatched 1 to 3 units, refused 956 to 672) are quoted from the DnaCalc commit message and the code comment; the 204 cells themselves were not re-read for this note, and the one Excel reading cited is a located capture cell (the same history asked with seasonality 0; the unit test asks it with 2 and holds the same value).
inferred: That Excel's own code builds the seven-point start series by this expression is inferred from the match; the five cells that differ by 1 to 3 units show the rounding of Excel's regression is not fully reproduced. Which Excel build the 204 cells came from is not stated in the commit.
